raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in parallel decode top-16 selector for MiniMax-M3.1 on gfx950, replacing the fixed FlyDSL w26 selector in the NVFP4 indexer.

Supersedes #65032, which was automatically closed when its target branch was deleted. This PR targets `main` and includes the review follow-up. The current update only renames the opt-in flag; kernel behavior, default and dispatch conditions are unchanged.

## Claims

- Preserve selected block IDs, ordering, tie handling and causal boundaries.
- Use runtime shape metadata to avoid new row/stride specializations during mixed-batch serving.
- Enable with `VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK=1`; default off. FP8 indexers, including C4 mono decode, bypass this path.

## Validation

### 900 s AgentX: baseline vs top-k only

4× MI355X, TP4, AgentX 1.0.12; **900 s per arm** after warmup. Model: `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` at `0a00e0e39fc00499b23efccc18a8ea63fce5c44c`. [InferenceX #4671](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4671) at `bed892b82`, DSpark K7, synthetic AL 4.04, seed 42.

Values are baseline → candidate. p90 interactivity uses `output_token_throughput_per_user.p10`; total throughput includes cached input tokens.

Run 1 uses `f9f83fb28`; the repeats use the same kernel in [eae2f1099](https://github.com/jiacao-amd/vllm/commit/eae2f1099c53654a2ede5e1fe35dad5b0a9021ad). Neither arm includes #62509. Each row is an independent pair.

| Comparison | p90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Output tok/s/GPU | Total tok/s/GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C16, run 1 | 139.67 → 149.73 (+7.20%) | 164.11 → 164.73 (+0.38%) | 19,470.28 → 19,566.95 (+0.50%) |
| C16, run 2 | 138.85 → 152.69 (+9.97%) | 164.59 → 166.63 (+1.24%) | 19,542.95 → 19,982.19 (+2.25%) |
| C32, run 1 | 83.67 → 91.13 (+8.91%) | 353.00 → 363.73 (+3.04%) | 46,831.45 → 48,283.98 (+3.10%) |
| C32, repeat (r3) | 87.18 → 91.26 (+4.68%) | 356.29 → 365.85 (+2.68%) | 47,237.91 → 48,630.29 (+2.95%) |

<details>
<summary>ITL and TTFT (baseline → candidate)</summary>

| Comparison | Mean ITL (ms) | p90 ITL (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | p90 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C16, run 1 | 5.221 → 5.302 | 7.158 → 6.669 | 540.663 → 517.630 | 875.833 → 920.976 |
| C16, run 2 | 5.100 → 4.682 | 7.193 → 6.547 | 559.563 → 527.167 | 983.740 → 921.735 |
| C32, run 1 | 8.307 → 7.906 | 11.947 → 10.965 | 703.343 → 698.839 | 1,374.336 → 1,267.423 |
| C32, repeat (r3) | 7.862 → 7.639 | 11.470 → 10.946 | 749.175 → 681.821 | 1,414.022 → 1,307.598 |

</details>

The first C32 repeat reached the 30 s drain limit with one cancelled request and is excluded. The table uses a fresh C32 pair with the same settings.

<details>
<summary>Configuration and reproduction</summary>

Pinned nightly: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:9cef62361792bd9cc621725c3af799993b6a68b6b62e3778dcf9b65ff6fcd872` (source `e0d00e4b8`). Both repetitions use this image.

C16/C32 use NVFP4 KV/indexer, V2 + DBO and a 32K prefill budget. Both arms include the same text-only DBO startup-guard fix (`supports_multimodal_inputs`). C4 uses FP8 KV/indexer, mono decode, an 8K prefill budget and no DBO.

Use the corresponding #4671 serving lane. Set `CONC` to the table's concurrency and `TOKENIZER` to the pinned model snapshot:

```bash
agentx profile --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tokenizer "$TOKENIZER" \
  --concurrency "$CONC" --benchmark-duration 900 \
  --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --server-metrics http://127.0.0.1:8000/metrics \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126
```

</details>

In-tree tests: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_index_topk_decode.py -k parallel_decode` — **78 passed**. Direct-kernel and host-dispatch comparisons cover exact FlyDSL ordering, ties, NaNs, causal boundaries, query lengths 1/4/8, fused/staged merge and strided outputs. Two-stream graph replays switch the same rows across adaptive/merge boundaries and verify zero counters after every replay. Pre-commit hooks passed.

Flag rename [c0e83e24b](https://github.com/jiacao-amd/vllm/commit/c0e83e24b43ef1f669d0f8829de1ec924aa890f9): environment parsing, recipe validation/rendering and pre-commit checks passed. The reported GPU, serving and accuracy results predate this name-only update; no GPU rerun was performed for the rename.

### GSM8K accuracy

Original scoring, all 1,319 questions per run; TP4/C16, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, reasoning effort low, 4096-token output limit, and real DSpark K7 block rejection.

Repeated evaluation: **two runs per arm**, using the same model revision and serving configuration above and one image rebuilt from main `380c8e438`, including the shared DBO startup fix. Candidate: the runtime diff from `8daa3c4c2` applied to that same base, with parallel top-k enabled; no tiles patch.

| Configuration | Run 1 correct / 1319 | Run 2 correct / 1319 | Mean accuracy | Mean delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 1,265 | 1,269 | 96.06% | — |
| Top-k only | 1,260 | 1,263 | 95.64% | -0.42 pp |

All four runs completed without API errors. Prefix-cache resets succeeded before every run; token-limit answers remain in the original scores.

Earlier single-pair GSM8K result: **1,267 → 1,264 correct (96.06% → 95.83%)**; invalid answers **1 → 0**.

## Details

Small `heads × rows <= 16` batches fuse selection and last-arriver merge; larger batches use staged merging. Scratch and counters are isolated by device, stream and shape.

The recipe adds opt-in `parallel_topk`; MI355 Buildkite kernel CI selects the new tests. Scoreboard enablement targets #4671's C16/C32 NVFP4 lane, `zip_override_tp4_dspark7.roles.agg.env`: set the flag to `"1"` in an image containing this patch and the text-only DBO startup fix noted above. Correctness CI does not enable serving; global default-on is not planned. Recipe validation, interactive command checks and documentation discovery passed.

Related work: #65087 optimizes the same NVFP4 selector by changing the existing FlyDSL kernel to four waves per row. This PR is an alternative opt-in Triton selector with partitioned workgroups and fused/staged merging; the reported gains exclude #65087. #59980 targets index scoring and #64264 targets kernel warmup.

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] PR checklist used; AI assistance disclosed.
- [x] Design fit, tests, documentation and CI coverage reviewed.
- [x] Requested performance validation and model evaluation complete.
- [ ] Attribute the observed GSM8K accuracy difference.
- [ ] Hosted CI complete.

</details>

@ChuanLi1101 Following up on your review in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65032#issuecomment-6567088515. This PR replaces #65032 after its base branch was deleted and now targets main.

- Added in-tree tests: 78 passed. Coverage includes exact FlyDSL ordering, ties/NaNs, causal boundaries, query lengths 1/4/8, and two-stream graph replays that switch rows between adaptive early-exit and merge paths. Counters are verified to reset after every replay.

- Repeated the 900s AgentX comparisons on the same pinned nightly. For C16/C32 respectively, output tok/s/GPU improved by 1.24%/2.68%, and p90 interactivity by 9.97%/4.68%. Both the original and repeated results are in the description.

- Renamed the flag to `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_1_PARALLEL_TOPK`, added recipe opt-in and MI355 correctness CI coverage. The default remains off.

- Documented scoreboard enablement: the InferenceX #4671 C16/C32 NVFP4 lane needs an image containing this patch and the documented DBO startup fix, with the flag explicitly enabled. That image rollout has not been performed.

The review fixes and measurements are included here; hosted CI remains pending the repository's pre-run gate.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", KINDS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "heads,reqs,query_len,max_seq_len",
+    [
+        (1, 16, 1, 1 << 20),
+        (1, 17, 1, 1 << 20),
+        (2, 2, 4, 1 << 20),
+        (2, 3, 4, 1 << 20),
+        (1, 2, 8, 1 << 20),
+        (1, 3, 8, 1 << 20),
+        (1, 2, 8, 0),
+        (1, 5, 4, 65536),
+    ],
+)
+def test_parallel_decode_matches_flydsl(
+    monkeypatch, kind, heads, reqs, query_len, max_seq_len
+):
+    """Both merge paths preserve FlyDSL ordering, causal masks and output guards."""
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.index_topk_decode.parallel_kernel import (
+        parallel_decode_topk,
+    )
+
+    rows = reqs * query_len
+    lengths = [1024 * BLOCK + query_len // 2, max_seq_len, 0, 1, 128, 65536]
+    seq = torch.tensor((lengths * reqs)[:reqs], dtype=torch.int32)
+    tok = torch.arange(rows) % query_len
+    live = (seq.repeat_interleave(query_len) - query_len + tok + 1).clamp(min=0)
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(4671)
+    scores = _scores(
+        kind, heads, rows, _width(max_seq_len), (live + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK, gen
+    )
+    storage = torch.empty(heads, rows + 7, scores.shape[-1], device="cuda")
+    score = storage[:, 3 : 3 + rows]
+    score.copy_(scores)
+    seq = seq.cuda()
+    results = []
+    for enabled in ("0", "1"):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK", enabled)
+        output, compared = _topk_out(heads, rows, pad=True)
+        minimax_m3_index_topk_decode_indices(
+            score, output, seq, max_seq_len=max_seq_len, query_len=query_len
+        )
+        results.append(compared)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(results[1], results[0], rtol=0, atol=0)
+    output, compared = _topk_out(heads, rows, pad=True)
+    cols = 64 if max_seq_len == 0 else _width(max_seq_len)
+    parallel_decode_topk(score, output, seq, query_len, cols)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(compared, results[0], rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("query_len", [1, 4, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fused", [True, False])
+def test_parallel_decode_graph_replay_resets_counters(monkeypatch, query_len, fused):
+    """Two streams change the same rows between direct selection and merge."""
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.index_topk_decode.parallel_kernel import (
+        _buffers,
+        parallel_decode_topk,
+    )
+
+    reqs = 2 if fused else 16 // query_len + 1
+    rows, cols = reqs * query_len, 8192
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(65032)
+    score = _scores("nan", 1, rows, cols, torch.full((rows,), cols), gen).cuda()
+    # The first length crosses the adaptive boundary within one verify request.
+    # Subsequent replays cross it in both directions and change active CTA count.
+    cases = [
+        [1024 * BLOCK + query_len // 2, cols * BLOCK],
+        [0, 1],
+        [cols * BLOCK, 512 * BLOCK],
+        [128 * BLOCK, 2049 * BLOCK],
+    ]
+    lengths = [
+        torch.tensor((case * reqs)[:reqs], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        for case in cases
+    ]
+    streams = [torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()]
+    graphs, inputs, outputs, counters = [], [], [], []
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK", "0")
+    for stream in streams:
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):

+            output, compared = _topk_out(1, rows, pad=True)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Parallel decode top-16 with runtime shape metadata.
+
+Merge widths cover the host's maximum 8192 score columns. Keeping
+rows, strides, and columns dynamic avoids compiling new kernels when
+mixed batches change their score layout during serving.
+"""
+
+import functools
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _flydsl_key(score, index, valid):
+    bits = score.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+    ordered = bits ^ ((bits >> 31) & 0x7FFFFFFF)
+    ordered = tl.where(
+        (ordered > 0x7F800000) | (ordered < -2139095041), -2139095041, ordered
+    )
+    key = (ordered.to(tl.int64) << 32) | index.to(tl.int64)
+    return tl.where(valid, key, -9223372036854775807 - 1)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["SH", "SR", "ROWS", "COLS", "PARTS", "OH", "OR"])
+def _m3_parallel_topk_partial(
+    score,
+    lengths,
+    partial,
+    output,
+    SH,
+    SR,
+    ROWS,
+    COLS,
+    QUERY: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS,
+    OH,
+    OR,
+    ADAPTIVE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row, head, part = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    seq = tl.load(lengths + row // QUERY)
+    live = tl.minimum(COLS, tl.cdiv(tl.maximum(0, seq - QUERY + row % QUERY + 1), 128))
+    if ADAPTIVE:  # noqa: SIM102
+        if live <= 1024:
+            if part != 0:
+                return
+            if live <= 128:
+                winners = _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, 128)
+            elif live <= 512:
+                winners = _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, 512)
+            else:
+                winners = _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, 1024)
+            rank = tl.arange(0, 16)
+            indices = tl.where(rank < live, winners & 0xFFFFFFFF, -1).to(tl.int32)
+            tl.store(output + head * OH + row * OR + rank, indices)
+            return
+    if part * CHUNK >= live:
+        return
+    index = part * CHUNK + tl.arange(0, CHUNK)
+    valid = index < live
+    values = tl.load(score + head * SH + row * SR + index, mask=valid, other=0)
+    winners = tl.topk(_flydsl_key(values, index, valid), 16)
+    out = ((head * ROWS + row) * PARTS + part) * 16 + tl.arange(0, 16)
+    tl.store(partial + out, winners)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["OH", "OR", "ROWS", "COLS", "PARTS"])
+def _m3_parallel_topk_merge(
+    partial,
+    lengths,
+    output,
+    OH,
+    OR,
+    ROWS,
+    COLS,
+    QUERY: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS,
+    MERGE: tl.constexpr,
+    ADAPTIVE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row, head = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1)
+    seq = tl.load(lengths + row // QUERY)
+    live = tl.minimum(COLS, tl.cdiv(tl.maximum(0, seq - QUERY + row % QUERY + 1), 128))
+    if ADAPTIVE:  # noqa: SIM102
+        if live <= 1024:
+            return
+    offset = tl.arange(0, MERGE)
+    keys = tl.load(
+        partial + (head * ROWS + row) * PARTS * 16 + offset,
+        mask=(offset < PARTS * 16) & (offset // 16 * CHUNK < live),
+        other=-9223372036854775807 - 1,
+    )
+    winners = tl.topk(keys, 16)
+    rank = tl.arange(0, 16)
+    indices = tl.where(rank < live, winners & 0xFFFFFFFF, -1).to(tl.int32)
+    tl.store(output + head * OH + row * OR + rank, indices)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["SH", "SR"])
+def _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, WIDTH: tl.constexpr):
+    index = tl.arange(0, WIDTH)
+    values = tl.load(score + head * SH + row * SR + index, mask=index < live, other=0)
+    return tl.topk(_flydsl_key(values, index, index < live), 16)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["SH", "SR", "OH", "OR", "ROWS", "COLS", "PARTS"])
+def _m3_parallel_topk_fused(
+    score,
+    lengths,
+    partial,
+    counters,
+    output,
+    SH,
+    SR,
+    OH,
+    OR,
+    ROWS,
+    COLS,
+    QUERY: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS,
+    MERGE: tl.constexpr,
+    ADAPTIVE: tl.constexpr,
+    COUNTER_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row, head, part = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    seq = tl.load(lengths + row // QUERY)
+    live = tl.minimum(COLS, tl.cdiv(tl.maximum(0, seq - QUERY + row % QUERY + 1), 128))
+    if ADAPTIVE:  # noqa: SIM102 -- remove unused branches at compile time
+        if live <= 1024:
+            if part != 0:
+                return
+            if live <= 128:
+                winners = _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, 128)
+            elif live <= 512:
+                winners = _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, 512)
+            else:
+                winners = _m3_row_topk(score, head, row, live, SH, SR, 1024)
+            rank = tl.arange(0, 16)
+            indices = tl.where(rank < live, winners & 0xFFFFFFFF, -1).to(tl.int32)
+            tl.store(output + head * OH + row * OR + rank, indices)
+            return
+    active = tl.maximum(1, tl.cdiv(live, CHUNK))
+    if part >= active:
+        return
+    index = part * CHUNK + tl.arange(0, CHUNK)
+    valid = index < live
+    values = tl.load(score + head * SH + row * SR + index, mask=valid, other=0)
+    winners = tl.topk(_flydsl_key(values, index, valid), 16)
+    rank = tl.arange(0, 16)
+    if active == 1:
+        indices = tl.where(rank < live, winners & 0xFFFFFFFF, -1).to(tl.int32)
+        tl.store(output + head * OH + row * OR + rank, indices)
+        return
+    out = ((head * ROWS + row) * PARTS + part) * 16 + rank
+    tl.store(partial + out, winners)
+    # The release publishes every CTA's partial; the last arrival acquires them.
+    counter = counters + (head * ROWS + row) * COUNTER_STRIDE
+    arrival = tl.atomic_add(counter, 1, sem="acq_rel", scope="gpu")
+    if arrival != active - 1:
+        return
+    offset = tl.arange(0, MERGE)
+    keys = tl.load(
+        partial + (head * ROWS + row) * PARTS * 16 + offset,
+        mask=offset < active * 16,
+        other=-9223372036854775807 - 1,
+        volatile=True,
+    )
+    winners = tl.topk(keys, 16)
+    indices = tl.where(rank < live, winners & 0xFFFFFFFF, -1).to(tl.int32)
+    tl.store(output + head * OH + row * OR + rank, indices)
+    tl.atomic_xchg(counter, 0, sem="acq_rel", scope="gpu")
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _buffers(heads, rows, cols, device_index, stream_id):
+    # Graphs retain these addresses. Each DBO stream owns separate counters.
+    device = torch.device("cuda", device_index)
+    chunk = 512 if heads * rows <= 16 else 256
+    return (
+        torch.empty(
+            (heads, rows, triton.cdiv(cols, chunk), 16),
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=device,
+        ),
+        torch.zeros((heads, rows), dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+    )
+
+
+def parallel_decode_topk(score, output, lengths, query_len, cols):
+    heads, rows, _ = score.shape
+    stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(score.device)
+    scratch, counters = _buffers(
+        heads, rows, cols, score.device.index, stream.cuda_stream
+    )
+    if heads * rows <= 16:
+        parts = triton.cdiv(cols, 512)
+        _m3_parallel_topk_fused[(rows, heads, parts)](
+            score,
+            lengths,
+            scratch,
+            counters,
+            output,
+            score.stride(0),
+            score.stride(1),
+            output.stride(0),
+            output.stride(1),
+            rows,
+            cols,
+            query_len,
+            512,
+            parts,
+            256,
+            True,
+            1,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+        return
+    parts = triton.cdiv(cols, 256)
+    _m3_parallel_topk_partial[(rows, heads, parts)](
+        score,
+        lengths,
+        scratch,
+        output,
+        score.stride(0),
+        score.stride(1),
+        rows,
+        cols,
+        query_len,
+        256,
+        parts,
+        output.stride(0),
+        output.stride(1),
+        True,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    _m3_parallel_topk_merge[(rows, heads)](
+        scratch,
+        lengths,
+        output,
+        output.stride(0),
+        output.stride(1),
+        rows,
+        cols,
+        query_len,
+        256,
+        parts,
+        512,
+        True,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )

@ChuanLi1101 Following up on your review in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65032#issuecomment-6567088515. This PR replaces #65032 after its base branch was deleted and now targets main.

- Added in-tree tests: 78 passed. Coverage includes exact FlyDSL ordering, ties/NaNs, causal boundaries, query lengths 1/4/8, and two-stream graph replays that switch rows between adaptive early-exit and merge paths. Counters are verified to reset after every replay.

- Repeated the 900s AgentX comparisons on the same pinned nightly. For C16/C32 respectively, output tok/s/GPU improved by 1.24%/2.68%, and p90 interactivity by 9.97%/4.68%. Both the original and repeated results are in the description.

- Renamed the flag to `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_1_PARALLEL_TOPK`, added recipe opt-in and MI355 correctness CI coverage. The default remains off.

- Documented scoreboard enablement: the InferenceX #4671 C16/C32 NVFP4 lane needs an image containing this patch and the documented DBO startup fix, with the flag explicitly enabled. That image rollout has not been performed.

The review fixes and measurements are included here; hosted CI remains pending the repository's pre-run gate.
